title: A Balance That Counts Electrons: Paramagnetism and the Spin-only Magnetic Moment
subject: Chemistry
objective: Every electron is a tiny magnet; in a pair the spins cancel, so only unpaired electrons make an ion paramagnetic. Count them from the ion's d configuration (singly up to d⁵, then pairing) and the spin-only formula gives the magnetic moment: μ = √(n(n+2)) BM, from 1.73 for one unpaired electron to 5.92 for Mn²⁺ (d⁵). A measured μ (Gouy balance) counts the unpaired electrons.

tf.explain: So μ depends only on the number of unpaired electrons.

tf.explain: μ = √8 = 2.84 BM; μ is not proportional to n.

ar.r: Zn²⁺ has a completely filled 3d¹⁰ configuration.
ar.explain: All paired, so there is no net moment.

ar.a: Mn²⁺ has a higher magnetic moment than Cu²⁺.
ar.r: Mn²⁺ has more d electrons than Cu²⁺.
ar.explain: Mn²⁺ (d⁵) has fewer d electrons than Cu²⁺ (d⁹); it has more UNPAIRED electrons (5 vs 1).

short.q: Why are most transition-metal ions paramagnetic?
short.solution: Their 3d orbitals are partly filled, so they hold unpaired electrons; each unpaired electron has a magnetic moment that is not cancelled by a partner of opposite spin.

short.q: How does a Gouy balance show that CuSO₄ is paramagnetic?
short.solution: The sample hangs between the poles of an electromagnet; when the field is switched on it is drawn into the field and appears heavier on the balance. The change gives the susceptibility, from which μ is found.

match.explain: Count n from the configuration, then μ = √(n(n+2)).
